root_cause.text: neigh_xmit() fails to free the socket buffer (skb) when the requested neighbor table is not registered, because the error path for an uninitialized table returns -EAFNOSUPPORT without calling kfree_skb(), and callers (like MPLS) ignore the return value, assuming the skb is always consumed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the `if (!tbl)` branch from `goto out_unlock` (which only unlocks RCU and returns `err` without freeing) to `rcu_read_unlock(); goto out_kfree_skb;`, ensuring the skb is freed. The CVE description and commit message explicitly state that the skb is leaked when the neighbor table is uninitialized, e.g., `NEIGH_ND_TABLE` when IPv6 is disabled.
